trial_court: Court of Additional District Judge (North), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi, Civil Appeal No.2012 of 2013
case_name: Shri Rakesh Raman vs Smt. Kavita
facts_of_case: The parties were married under Hindu rituals and customs in Delhi on April 16, 1994. The husband's case is that his wife was not happy in their small dwelling and used offensive language against him. She left her matrimonial home several times, including in September 1994 when she got her pregnancy terminated without informing her husband.

legal_principles.principle: Repeatedly filing of criminal cases by one party against the other in a matrimonial matter would amount to cruelty.
legal_principles.held: A three Judge Bench of this Court in Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli1 held that repeatedly filing of criminal cases by one party against the other in a matrimonial matter would amount to cruelty and the same was reiterated by a Division Bench of this Court in K. Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa2.
cited_cases: Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli, (2006) 4 SCC 558
K. Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa

legal_principles.principle: Mere filing of criminal cases against the husband would not constitute cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The High Court has taken a view that mere filing of criminal cases against the appellant−husband would not constitute cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The marriage was dissolved by the order of the trial court, which was set aside by the Delhi High Court and the petition of the husband was dismissed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on matrimonial disputes in Delhi
